intro_html:
Lasagna usually shows up on the ledger as a splurge night, all that ricotta and heavy cream doing a number on both your macros and your wallet. This one flips the math. We blend cottage cheese straight into the alfredo so you get that same creamy, layered comfort without the ricotta bill, and we lean on plain boneless skinless chicken breast for the muscle. The result lands at {{protein}} grams of protein and {{cal}} calories a serving, which is the kind of number that lets you eat lasagna on a Tuesday and still call it meal prep.

Here is the honest part. This is not a from-scratch, all-afternoon lasagna. It is a smart-shortcut lasagna built to feed you across a whole work week for pocket change. You lean on a jar of alfredo and no-boil noodles to skip the fussy steps, and you put the savings and the effort where they actually show up, which is the protein and the price per serving.

Fourteen dinners that each clear {{protein}} grams of protein for that price is the kind of deal the takeout menu cannot touch, and you already know exactly what went into it.
shop_smart:
The chicken breast is the biggest line on this list, so buy it the way it is cheapest in your store: the family pack by the pound almost always beats the small tray, and what you do not use freezes flat. The cottage cheese is the star buy here, and it is doing the job ricotta usually charges double for. You need 4 2/3 cups, so grab the big tub rather than the little cups and you will use it up. Full fat or low fat both work; low fat trims the fat number without hurting the creaminess once it is blended smooth.

For the alfredo you only need 1 3/4 cups, so a single standard jar covers the batch with room to spare. Buy a jar you would actually eat by the spoonful, because it carries a lot of the flavor. The fresh mozzarella runs 1 lb 2 1/2 oz and the parmesan 2 1/3 cups grated. If your store sells parmesan by the wedge and you own a grater, that is the move for freshness, but a tub of the pre-grated works fine and saves you the arm workout.
make_it:
Heat the oven to 425 degrees. Roast the chicken breast on a sheet pan until it reaches 165 degrees in the thickest part, about 20 to 25 minutes, then let it rest and roughly chop it into bite-size pieces. Set the chicken aside.

Make the sauce in one pass: blend the cottage cheese, the alfredo, and a generous pinch of salt and black pepper together until it is completely smooth. That blend is what replaces the fussy ricotta layer, so do not skip the smooth part.

Now build it. Coat the bottom of your baking dish with a thin layer of the blended sauce so nothing sticks. Lay down noodles, then another layer of sauce, then chopped chicken, a scatter of parsley, mozzarella, and parmesan. Repeat the layers until everything is used, keeping parsley on the first couple of layers only and finishing the top with mozzarella and parmesan. Cover and bake 30 minutes, then uncover and bake another 10 to 15 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and browning at the edges. Garnish with fresh parsley and a little grated parmesan, then let it rest at least 5 minutes before you slice.
portion_html:
Fourteen servings out of one bake, and the fair way to split lasagna is by weight, not by eyeballing squares. Weigh your empty baking dish before you build, then weigh it again full and hot out of the oven. Subtract the dish, divide what is left by 14, and that is your target grams per container. Scoop to the scale, not to the spoon.

Lasagna slices firm up as they cool, so if you let it rest and chill fully before portioning you will get cleaner blocks that stack neatly in your containers. Reheat covered so the noodles stay tender and the cheese comes back to life instead of drying out.
